title: The Mansion of Death and the Red Wall
notes: This is a 4-part case (episodes 558-561) but only subtitle transcripts for 558 and 561 were found locally in subs_resolved/ -- 559 and 560 are missing. Episode 561 opens with an in-show recap that covers most of the missing middle (formal alibi-check of the three surviving mansion residents, Naoki Shirou's murder, Morofushi's solo investigation, the mansion fire, his rescue by Uehara), so the surviving evidence chain is largely reconstructable, but any finer-grained interrogation dialogue from 559-560 is not represented here. Detective-cast regulars (Kogoro, Ran, Conan, Haibara, Agasa) omitted by convention; Conan's specific deductive interjections during the finale are folded into the edges/clues they produced rather than attributed to a Conan node. Discrepancies vs. the old cases/ file: (1) it renders both victim-2 and the culprit's names in reversed (given-name-first) order -- 'Shiro Naoki' should be Naoki Shirou (surname Naoki, given name Shirou) and 'Naoki Midorikawa' should be Midorikawa Naoki (surname Midorikawa, given name Naoki) -- this reversal is exactly the point of the dying-message trick (the katakana word 'Naoki' is ambiguous between Naoki Shirou's surname and Midorikawa Naoki's given name), so getting the name order right matters for the puzzle itself; (2) the old file's has_motive_against edge left the motive as 'unspecified,' but the transcript gives a clear one: Midorikawa's rage at discovering Akashi had painted over an old portrait of his late wife Aoi to reuse the canvas, compounded by seeing an unfinished new portrait of her half-burnt in the yard the day after her death. The old file's culprit identification (s1/Midorikawa) itself was correct. case_type: murder.

attrs.backstory: elementary-school classmate and lifelong rival of Morofushi

clues.desc: Sit on the white chair facing the red wall, then the black chair facing the white wall (chess order): red's complementary afterimage, green, appears -- Midorikawa's color.

The victim left the dying message at scene 1, but the same red wall appeared at scene 2 -- since the culprit wouldn't restage a message they didn't fully understand, a third party (Shirou) must have altered scene 1 first.

Fingerprints on the storage room doorknob and spray can, assumed to be the victim's, actually matched Inspector Morofushi -- he touched them while first discovering the body, not while committing the crime.

edges.method: starvation, locked in the storage room
